provenance.paper: McCarthy, J. (1980). Circumscription — a form of non-monotonic reasoning.
provenance.locus: Section 4 (blocks/bird examples): minimizing ab; birds fly unless abnormal, penguins are abnormal with respect to flying.
provenance.notes: Canonical bird/penguin instance of circumscribing the abnormality predicate. Tweety is a bird with no abnormality evidence (flies entailed in all ab-minimal models); Opus is a penguin (penguin forces ab_bird_opus, so flies_opus is NOT entailed even though naive monotone chaining ignoring not_-premises would derive it).

input.intent: circumscribe abnormality over the bird/penguin theory

expected.notes: The unique ab-minimal model has exactly {ab_bird_opus}: penguin_opus forces it, while ab_bird_tweety stays false by minimization, so flies_tweety holds and flies_opus does not.
